===Overall team records===
The system used in the European Championship up to 1992 was 2 points for a win, and [[Three points for a win|3 points for a win]] from 1996 onwards. In this ranking 3 points are awarded for a win, 1 for a draw and 0 for a loss. As per statistical convention in football, matches decided in [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] are counted as wins and losses, while matches decided by [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-outs]] are counted as draws. Teams are ranked by total points, then by goal difference, then by goals scored.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co36/records-all-time-table/|title=EURO » All-time league table|website=WorldFootball.net|access-date=10 July 2024}}</ref>

===Hosts===
From [[1960 European Nations' Cup|1960]] to [[UEFA Euro 1976|1976]] the host was decided between one of the four semi-finalists. Since [[UEFA Euro 1980|1980]] the hosts have automatically qualified, except in [[UEFA Euro 2020|2020]] when every country had to qualify through qualification. Germany has hosted the finals in [[UEFA Euro 2024|2024]].

===Countries that have never qualified===
{{see also|UEFA European Championship qualifying}}

The following teams are current or former UEFA members which have never qualified for the European Championship. Of these, Bosnia and Herzegovina ([[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]], [[2026 FIFA World Cup|2026]]) and Israel ([[1970 FIFA World Cup|1970]]) are the only teams to qualify for the [[FIFA World Cup]], though Israel did so as an [[Asian Football Confederation]] (AFC) member.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co1172/records-all-time-table/ |title=EURO Qualifiers » All-time league table |website=WorldFootball.net |access-date=21 November 2019}}</ref> [[Saarland national football team|Saarland]] didn't exist by 1960 when the European Championship was introduced and East Germany, that qualified to the FIFA World Cup in [[1974 FIFA World Cup|1974]], never qualified for the European Championship until it ceased to exist in 1990.

'''Legend'''
*{{border|width=1px|color=gray|&nbsp;•&nbsp;}} – Did not qualify
*{{border|width=1px|color=gray|&nbsp;×&nbsp;}} – Did not enter / Withdrew / Banned
*{{border|width=3px|color=red|&nbsp; &nbsp;}} – Co-host of the final tournament

===Goalscoring===
; Most goals scored in a tournament: 142 goals, [[UEFA Euro 2020|2020]]<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/news/026a-12a12861a321-17e294c3aa1f-1000--euro-2020-smashes-goal-record/ |title=EURO 2020 smashes finals goal records |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=11 July 2021 |access-date=11 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628230651/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/news/026a-12a12861a321-17e294c3aa1f-1000--euro-2020-smashes-goal-record/ |archive-date=28 June 2021 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
; Fewest goals scored in a tournament: 7 goals, [[UEFA Euro 1968|1968]]
; Fewest goals scored in a tournament (since 1980): 27 goals, [[UEFA Euro 1980|1980]]
; Most goals per match in a tournament: 4.75 goals per match, [[UEFA Euro 1976|1976]]
; Most goals per match in a tournament (since 1980): 2.78 goals per match, [[UEFA Euro 2020|2020]]
; Fewest goals per match in a tournament: 1.4 goals per match, [[UEFA Euro 1968|1968]]
; Fewest goals per match in a tournament (since 1980): 1.93 goals per match, [[UEFA Euro 1980|1980]]
; Most scorers in a tournament: 85, [[UEFA Euro 2024|2024]]
; Most players scoring at least two goals in a tournament: 30, [[UEFA Euro 2020|2020]]
; Most players scoring at least three goals in a tournament: 13, [[UEFA Euro 2020|2020]]
; Most players scoring at least four goals in a tournament: 6, [[UEFA Euro 2020|2020]]
; Most players scoring at least five goals in a tournament: 2, [[UEFA Euro 2000|2000]], [[UEFA Euro 2020|2020]]

==Teams==

===All-time===

; Fastest penalty converted: 118 seconds, [[Robbie Brady]] ({{fb|IRL}} vs {{fb|FRA|1974}}, [[UEFA Euro 2016|2016]])<ref> {{cite web|title=Ireland's Robbie Brady made Euros history vs France| url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/row-zed/irelands-robbie-brady-made-euros-8286124 |website=Daily Mirror| date=26 June 2016 |access-date=15 June 2024}}</ref>
; Fastest goal by a substitute: 1 minute, [[Alessandro Altobelli]] ({{fb|ITA|1946}} vs {{fb|DEN}}, [[UEFA Euro 1988|1988]]); [[Juan Carlos Valerón]] ({{fb|ESP}} vs {{fb|RUS}}, [[UEFA Euro 2004|2004]]); [[Ondrej Duda]] ({{fb|SVK}} vs {{fb|WAL}}, [[UEFA Euro 2016|2016]]); [[Ferran Torres]] ({{fb|ESP}} vs {{fb|SVK}}, [[UEFA Euro 2020|2020]])
; Fastest goal, knockout stage: 57 seconds, [[Merih Demiral]] ({{fb|TUR}} vs {{fb|AUT}}, [[UEFA Euro 2024|2024]])<ref>{{cite web |last=Fitzpatrick |first=Peter |url=https://onefootball.com/fr/news/demiral-makes-euros-knockout-history-with-rapid-quick-goal-vs-austria-39708672 |title=Demiral makes EUROs knockout history with rapid-quick goal vs Austria 😲 |publisher=OneFootball |date=2 July 2024 }}</ref>
; Fastest goal in a final: 2 minutes, [[Luke Shaw]] ({{fb|ENG}} vs {{fb|ITA}}, [[UEFA Euro 2020|2020]])
; Fastest goal in the second half: 21 seconds, [[Marcel Coraș]] ({{fb|ROU|1965}} vs {{fb|FRG}}, [[UEFA Euro 1984|1984]])<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0254-0d7b2ee06671-b5cd8c1dcd92-1000--voller-double-for-west-germany-downs-romania-in-euro-1984-gr/ |title=Völler double for West Germany downs Romania in EURO 1984 Group 2 |publisher=UEFA |date=4 October 2003 }}</ref>

; Latest goal in regulation time: 90+10th minute, [[Kevin Csoboth]] ({{fb|HUN}} vs {{fb|SCO}}, [[UEFA Euro 2024|2024]])<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c899z89p7d4t |title=Scotland 0-1 Hungary: Euro 2024 over for Steve Clarke's side after stoppage-time goal |work=BBC Sport|date=23 June 2024|access-date=24 June 2024 }}</ref>
; Latest goal from kickoff: 120+2nd minute, [[Semih Şentürk]] ({{fb|TUR}} vs {{fb|CRO}}, [[UEFA Euro 2008|2008]])
; Latest winning goal from kickoff: 120+1st minute, [[Artem Dovbyk]] ({{fb|UKR}} vs {{fb|SWE}}, [[UEFA Euro 2020|2020]])
; Latest goal from kickoff in a final: 113th minute, [[Viktor Ponedelnik]] ({{fb|URS}} vs {{fb|YUG}}, [[1960 European Nations' Cup final|1960]])
; Latest goal from kickoff, with no goals scored in between: 119th minute, [[Ivan Klasnić]] ({{fb|CRO}} vs {{fb|TUR}}, [[UEFA Euro 2008|2008]])
; Latest goal from kickoff in final, with no goals scored in between: 109th minute, [[Eder (Portuguese footballer)|Eder]] ({{fb|POR}} vs {{fb|FRA|1974}}, [[UEFA Euro 2016 final|2016]])

====Own goals====
{{main|List of UEFA European Championship own goals}}

As of the 2024 tournament, 30 own goals have been scored. France have been the beneficiary of five own goals, while three have been conceded by Portuguese, Slovak and Turkish players. No player has scored more than one own goal.

; Most assists: 7, [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] ({{fb|POR}}, 2004–2024)
